node.title: Do we grandfather existing annual plans?
node.body: Moving annual customers to usage pricing at renewal risks Q4 churn. Do we keep their price for a year?

node.title: The usage tier carries 3x the support load
node.body:
Six weeks of beta tickets show the usage tier generating three times the support volume of annual plans, and almost none of it is about the bill itself.

- Mostly onboarding confusion, not billing disputes
- Drops to 1.4x after a customer's second month
- Concentrated in teams under 10 seats

node.title: Grandfather annual plans for 12 months, then migrate at renewal
node.body:
Existing annual customers keep their current price until their first renewal after 1 March, then move to usage pricing with a one-off credit worth two months of their old plan. This keeps the Q4 churn risk low and gives support a year to fix the onboarding confusion behind most usage-tier tickets.

#### What this means

- Two price books run side by side until the last grandfathered plan renews
- Finance signs off the credit amount before the migration email goes out
- Sales stops quoting the lifetime-deal tier from today

```
{ "plan": "annual-2025", "override": "grandfathered" }
```

text:
Before we settle this, check each of these with the team:

1. Whether annual plans really sell better once the discount is gone.
2. Whether the trial numbers hold for teams as well as single seats.
3. Whether finance can live with a floor price on the smallest plan.
4. Who owns the regional overrides, and how often they change.
5. What the support team hears most in the first week after signup.
6. Which of the three onboarding steps people skip most often.
7. Whether the plan picker needs a recommended option at all.
8. What happens to existing customers when the packaging changes.
9. How the new names read next to the old ones in the invoices.
10. Whether the price page needs a comparison table or only a list.
11. What we tell sales about the transition period and its end date.
12. Who signs off on the final wording before it goes live.
